exposure: offspring birth weight patterns across consecutive pregnancies (first and second birth)
changes in offspring birth weight quartiles (Q1, Q2/Q3, Q4)
cohort: The study included women with spontaneous and iatrogenic term deliveries in Norway between 1967 and 2020 who had at least two births.
finding: Changes in offspring birth weight patterns across consecutive pregnancies were associated with long-term maternal CVD mortality; specifically, a lower birth weight in the second infant (Q1) increased mortality risk, while a higher birth weight (Q4) decreased risk compared to Q2/Q3.
mod_finding: The observed patterns of maternal CVD mortality risk related to birth weight changes were similar for women with iatrogenic and spontaneous deliveries.
followup_time: Follow-up for maternal CVD mortality occurred until 2020 for women who delivered between 1967 and 2020.
birth_weight: Offspring birth weight was standardized and combined with gestational age to form birth weight quartiles (Q1, Q2/Q3, Q4).
gest_age: The study included term deliveries, and gestational age was used in combination with standardized birth weight to form quartiles.
